words.sentence: Ramesh is a very \(\underline{\text{dubious}}\) character.
words.solution: The word 'dubious' means hesitating or doubting; its antonym is 'trustworthy' — certain and reliable. Matches option C: trustworthy.

words.sentence: The confectioner \(\underline{\text{dusted}}\) a fine layer of sugar on the muffin.
words.solution: Here dusted means sprinkled a fine powder over something. Scattered, sprinkled and powdered all say much the same. Cleaned (removing a layer from a surface) is the opposite of covering it with a layer, so it is the answer.

words.sentence: Her \(\underline{\text{dynamic}}\) nature impressed everyone.
words.solution: Dynamic means characterized by constant change and progress; 'evolutionary' is nearest in meaning as it implies development and change. Matches option C: evolutionary.
"Eagerly" means with strong desire or enthusiasm, which is "keenly". "Stringently" means strictly, "dubiously" means doubtfully, and "playfully" means in a light-hearted way.
Earnestly means seriously and sincerely. Wordily and verbosely mean using too many words; ambiguously means unclearly.

words.sentence: We caught him \(\underline{\text{eavesdropping}}\) outside the window.
words.solution: Answer: C. 'Eavesdropping' = secretly listening to others' private conversation. 'Listening secretly' is the exact synonym.
Ebullient means cheerful and full of energy, so enthusiastic is the synonym.

words.sentence: Her ideas have always been \(\underline{\text{eccentric}}\).
words.solution: 'Eccentric' means unconventional or odd; its antonym is 'normal'. Option B (strange) is a synonym. Matches option C: normal.

words.sentence: In those days many monarchs enjoyed vast \(\underline{\text{ecclesiastical}}\) powers.
words.solution: Answer: B. 'Ecclesiastical' means relating to the church/spiritual matters; its opposite is 'temporal' (worldly/secular).

words.sentence: The news gave him inexpressible \(\underline{\text{ecstasy}}\).
words.solution: Ecstasy is overwhelming joy. Its opposite is depression, a state of deep sadness and low spirits. Delight is close to ecstasy, passion is strong feeling, and disappointment (sadness at an unmet hope) is milder and not the direct opposite of intense joy.

words.sentence: The poems of Kabir are \(\underline{\text{ecstatic}}\) in nature.
words.solution: The key concept is synonym identification. 'Ecstatic' means feeling intense happiness or elation; 'rapturous' means expressing great enthusiasm or delight. Matches option C: rapturous.

words.sentence: I fully believe that the cornerstone of good policy is an electorate that is \(\underline{\text{educated}}\) on the national issues.
words.solution: The antonym of 'educated' (knowledgeable/informed) is 'ignorant' (lacking knowledge). 'Cerebral' and 'erudite' are near-synonyms; 'enlightened' is also similar. Matches option C: ignorant.
To "efface" is to erase or wipe out a mark or memory, so "destroy" is the nearest meaning. "Hidden" only means out of sight, and "makeup" and "daily" are unrelated.

words.sentence: \(\underline{\text{Efficacy}}\) of the project needs an examination.
words.solution: Answer: A. 'Efficacy' means effectiveness/ability to produce a desired result. Its antonym is 'Inefficiency'. (Efficiency and Effectiveness are synonyms.)
"Effrontery" is shameless boldness or insolence, which is "audacity". "Politeness", "shyness" and "courtesy" are the opposite.

words.sentence: She was \(\underline{\text{effusive}}\) in her praise.
options: expressing approval while exhibiting strong feelings
words.solution: Answer: A. Effusive means expressing feelings in an unrestrained, gushing way — expressing approval while exhibiting strong feelings.

words.sentence: The judge ruled on the \(\underline{\text{egregious}}\) violations of human rights by the authorities.
words.solution: Egregious means outstandingly bad - so conspicuous that it cannot be overlooked. Flagrant carries exactly that sense of glaring, open wrongdoing. Subtle, inadvertent and concealed all run in the opposite direction, describing wrongs that are hidden or unintended.

words.sentence: She was \(\underline{\text{elated}}\) about her promotion, but her colleague felt quite disheartened.
words.solution: Elated means very happy and excited. Delighted and cheerful are synonyms; discouraged (dispirited, as the sentence's "disheartened" also signals) is the opposite.

words.sentence: His **eloquent** speech always persuades people to work for their betterment.
words.solution: Eloquent means fluent and persuasive in speaking; articulate means able to express ideas clearly and effectively. Vague and inarticulate are near-opposites; short is unrelated.

words.sentence: He speaks \(\underline{\text{eloquently}}\) and can pull crowds.
words.solution: Answer: A. 'Eloquently' means fluently and persuasively; its opposite is 'confusingly'. The other options are synonyms.
"Elucidate" means to make clear or explain, so "clarify". "Confuse", "darken" and "complicate" all mean the opposite.

words.sentence: There are many \(\underline{\text{elusive}}\) questions in philosophy
words.solution: Synonym of 'elusive' (difficult to grasp or define) is 'baffling'. Matches option B: baffling.

words.sentence: Wars leave behind a large number of \(\underline{\text{emaciated}}\) soldiers in the camps of both the victorious and the vanquished.
words.solution: Answer: A. 'Emaciated' means abnormally thin/wasted; its opposite is 'hefty' (large and heavy).

words.sentence: \(\underline{\text{Emboldened}}\) by its success, the leader now plans to go ahead with the plan and implementation.
words.solution: Answer: A. To embolden is to give courage or confidence. 'Emboldened by its success' means encouraged by it, so the nearest word is 'Encouraged'.

words.sentence: Many people love to visit \(\underline{\text{enchanting}}\) hills.
words.solution: Enchanting means delightfully charming or attractive; alluring means powerfully attractive. Risky, echoing and cool do not mean charming.
An encomium is a speech or piece of writing that praises someone highly. Panegyric, praise and tribute are near-synonyms; castigation (severe criticism or reprimand) is the opposite.

words.sentence: Some people complain when they \(\underline{\text{encounter}}\) a small misfortune in the course of their thoroughly happy life.
words.solution: The word 'encounter' means to come across or meet unexpectedly; among the options, 'run into' (to meet by chance) is the closest synonym. Matches option A: run into.

words.sentence: Her mother always \(\underline{\text{encouraged}}\) the idea of early marriage.
words.solution: To encourage an idea is to support it; the opposite is to discourage it. Motivated, supported and cheered are all near-synonyms of encouraged.

words.sentence: Words of \(\underline{\text{endearment}}\) always touch me.
words.solution: Answer: B. Endearment expresses affection/fondness.

words.sentence: The leader's \(\underline{\text{endurance}}\) paid and he won the elections.
words.solution: Answer: A. Endurance is the capacity to persist/withstand — nearest to patience.
The opposite of an enemy is a friend. Attacker and combatant are close to enemy, and a colleague is simply a co-worker.

words.sentence: The hot sun \(\underline{\text{enervated}}\) the labourer to the extent that he collapsed.
words.solution: To enervate is to drain of energy, to weaken; the labourer collapsed. Energise is close to its opposite, alleviate means to ease, and elevate means to raise.

words.sentence: Any classroom should provide an \(\underline{\text{engaging}}\) environment for learners.
words.solution: Answer: B. Engaging means attractive/interesting/holding attention; 'appealing' is the nearest in meaning.
"Enhance" means to improve or increase in quality. Its opposite is "impair", to weaken or damage. "Enrich" is a near synonym; "miracle" and "relevance" are unrelated nouns.

words.sentence: The artist's abstract painting was \(\underline{\text{enigmatic}}\) to the viewers.
words.solution: "Enigmatic" means mysterious and hard to understand; its opposite is "clear". "Mysterious" is a synonym, "instigating" means provoking, and "thrilling" means exciting.
"Enormous" means very large; its opposite is "minute" (very tiny). "Tremendous" and "monstrous" are near-synonyms, and "strong" is about strength, not size.

words.sentence: The teacher asked her students to understand the \(\underline{\text{ensuing}}\) problems and address them suitably.
words.solution: Answer: C. Ensuing = following, coming afterward, subsequent. Antonym is retrospective (looking back / relating to the past). (Subsequent and consequent are synonyms; en suite is unrelated.)

To "entail" is to involve something as a necessary part or result, that is, to "necessitate" it: "The job entails long hours." "Assume" means suppose, "eliminate" means remove, and "flaw" is a defect.
Entire means whole or complete, so its opposite is incomplete. Undivided and thorough are close in meaning; ingress means entry.

Envious means resentful of what others have, a grudging, mean-spirited feeling. Generous (glad to give and to see others do well) is its opposite. Suspicious, untrustworthy and malicious are all negative traits, not opposites.

words.sentence: Social media trends are \(\underline{\text{ephemeral}}\).
words.solution: Answer: A. 'Ephemeral' means short-lived; its opposite is 'everlasting' (the others are synonyms of ephemeral).
"Epistemic" means relating to knowledge or to the degree to which something is known (from the Greek "episteme", knowledge). It has nothing to do with the physical, the symbolic or space.

Besides "a perfect example", epitome means a summary or abridgement of a longer work. The opposite of an abridgement is an expansion. Precise and lucid are adjectives and exhort is a verb, so none of them can be the opposite of a noun meaning summary.

words.sentence: She accepted the prospect of her medical treatment with \(\underline{\text{equanimity}}\).
words.solution: Answer: B. Equanimity means calmness and composure. The opposite is agitation; tranquillity, composure and placidity are synonyms.

words.sentence: During the trial, the witness's deposition was \(\underline{\text{equivocal}}\).
words.solution: Equivocal means open to more than one interpretation - deliberately ambiguous or unclear. Its opposite is explicit: stated clearly and in detail, leaving no room for doubt. Ambiguous is a synonym of equivocal, not an antonym, while evasive and guarded describe the same reluctance to commit to a plain statement.
"Erroneous" means wrong or mistaken, as does "fallacious". "Right" and "accurate" are opposites, and "vital" means essential.
Erudite means having or showing great learning. Scholarly, learned and intellectual are near-synonyms; uninformed (lacking knowledge) is the opposite.

words.sentence: The writer's \(\underline{\text{erudition}}\) in science is revealed in every page of the book.
words.solution: Answer: B. 'Erudition' means deep learning/knowledge; its opposite is 'ignorance' (a noun, matching the noun erudition).
Esoteric means understood by only a small group with special knowledge. Its opposite is common (widely known). "Arcane", "mystical" and "obscure" are close in meaning to esoteric.
"Eternal" means lasting forever, without end, so "infinite" is the synonym. "Temporary", "fleeting" and "brief" all mean lasting a short time, the opposite.
A eulogy is a speech or piece of writing that praises someone, often someone who has died: a tribute. Criticism, insult and condemnation are close to its opposite.
To evaluate is to judge the worth, quality or amount of something, which is exactly what assess means. Unity is unrelated, and misquote and misjudge mean getting something wrong.

words.sentence: It was \(\underline{\text{evident}}\) from his gestures that he was feeling guilty.
words.solution: Evident means plain to see or obvious; its opposite is hidden. Visible is a synonym, and profuse and correct are unrelated.
To evoke is to bring a feeling or memory to mind, to call forth or produce it; induce (bring about) is closest. Abandon, reduce and divert do not mean this.
Exceptional means unusually good, outstanding. Trivial is nearly its opposite; emotional and total are unrelated.

words.sentence: He drank \(\underline{\text{excessive}}\) amount of liquor.
words.solution: Answer: B. Excessive = inordinate (immoderate, beyond proper limits). 'Unreasonable' is weaker and not standard for quantity; 'inordinate' is the precise synonym.

words.sentence: The young are easily \(\underline{\text{excitable}}\) when presented with strong emotional triggers.
words.solution: 'Excitable' means easily stirred up emotionally; its antonym is 'composed' (calm and collected). Matches option A: composed.

words.sentence: The church decided to \(\underline{\text{excommunicate}}\) him for his actions.
words.solution: 'Excommunicate' means to officially exclude from membership of a church; the nearest synonym is 'expel'. Matches option C: expel.

words.sentence: The experience of Covid Pandemic was \(\underline{\text{excruciating}}\) for much of the population.
words.solution: 'Excruciating' means intensely painful or agonizing; its antonym is 'mild' (gentle, not severe). Matches option D: mild.
"Exculpate" means to clear someone of blame or guilt, so "exonerate". "Condemn", "blame" and "punish" are the opposite of clearing someone (compare "culpable", guilty).

words.sentence: I plan and \(\underline{\text{execute}}\).
words.solution: The synonym of 'execute' (to carry out a plan) is 'accomplish' (to achieve/complete). Matches option C: accomplish.

words.sentence: The soldier showed an \(\underline{\text{exemplary}}\) courage.
words.solution: Answer: C. "Exemplary" means serving as a desirable model / ideal worthy of imitation; nearest synonym is "ideal". "Flawed" and "faulty" are opposite.

words.sentence: One's actions \(\underline{\text{exemplify}}\) one's attitude and values.
words.solution: Answer: D. 'Exemplify' means to illustrate/show by example; 'demonstrate' is nearest in meaning.

words.sentence: At the end of the marathon everybody was \(\underline{\text{exhausted}}\).
words.solution: 'Exhausted' means drained of energy; tired out. Matches option D: tired.

words.sentence: Winning the World Cup was the most \(\underline{\text{exhilarating}}\) moment for the Indian cricket team.
words.solution: Answer: C. 'Exhilarating' means making one feel very happy, animated, or thrilled. The nearest in meaning is 'thrilling'.

words.sentence: The party leader \(\underline{\text{exhorted}}\) his members to start preparing for the formation of their government.
words.solution: Answer: B. 'Exhorted' = strongly encouraged/urged. 'Urged' is the nearest synonym. 'Discouraged' is the opposite.
Exiguous means very small in amount, meagre (exiguous resources). Scanty is the synonym. Huge, excessive and abundant all mean the opposite.
To "exonerate" is to declare someone free from blame or guilt. Its opposite is "convict", to declare someone guilty. "Free", "excuse" and "liberate" are close in meaning to exonerate.

words.sentence: He has been \(\underline{\text{exonerated}}\) as he tendered an apology.
words.solution: Answer: C. 'Exonerated' means cleared of blame or absolved. Its opposite is 'convicted' (found guilty). 'pardoned' is a synonym; 'honoured' and 'felicitated' are unrelated.

words.sentence: The shopkeeper is known to charge \(\underline{\text{exorbitant}}\) rates for the articles in his shop.
words.solution: Answer: B. Exorbitant means unreasonably expensive, so affordable is its opposite. High, outrageous and ridiculous all point the same way as the underlined word.
Expertise is expert skill or knowledge in a field; proficiency is a high degree of skill. Clumsiness, lack and ignorance point the other way.

words.sentence: The committee wanted us to \(\underline{\text{explain}}\) this in detail.
words.solution: To elaborate is to explain or describe in more detail, which matches "explain this in detail". Trouble, collect and keen do not mean explain.

words.sentence: There is \(\underline{\text{exponential}}\) growth in the development of the scientific researches in the recent few decades.
words.solution: 'Exponential' means increasing rapidly or at a very fast rate. Its antonym is 'meager' (very small in amount). Matches option C: meager.

words.sentence: Temperature is a measure of internal energy of an object and is frequently \(\underline{\text{expressed}}\) by physicists in units of Kelvin.
words.solution: The antonym of 'expressed' (conveyed, made known) is 'concealed' (hidden, kept secret). Matches option D: concealed.

words.sentence: All the allegations against the actor were \(\underline{\text{expunged}}\) by the committee of inquiry.
words.solution: Answer: C. Expunge = to erase/remove/strike out completely. Antonym is accepted (retained/admitted on record). 'Got rid of' is a synonym; 'rejected' here would also mean dismissing the allegations, which aligns with removal, so accepted is the cleaner opposite.

words.sentence: His speech was full of emotions and it was an \(\underline{\text{extempore}}\).
words.solution: Answer: A. Extempore = spoken without preparation, impromptu, unrehearsed. Antonym is prepared. (Unrehearsed and ad lib are synonyms; ready made is also a near-synonym in the prepared-in-advance sense, but 'prepared' is the direct antonym of impromptu.)
"Extinct" means no longer existing, died out. "Vanished" (disappeared completely) is closest. Vibrant, active and living are opposites.
To extirpate is to root out or destroy completely. Exterminate, uproot and eradicate are synonyms; establish (set up, plant firmly) is the opposite.
To extol is to praise highly. Reward means to give something in return for merit, which is not the same as praising, and punish and dismay are unrelated.

words.sentence: \(\underline{\text{Extradition}}\) of the leader of the group was debated for hours in the meeting.
words.solution: Answer: D. Extradition is the surrender/handing over of a person to another jurisdiction; 'deportation' (removal/sending away) is the nearest in meaning among the options.
Exuberance is lively energy and enthusiasm, which is vibrancy. Laziness is close to its opposite; sympathy and impartiality are unrelated.

words.sentence: The crowd gave an \(\underline{\text{exultant}}\) cheer to the football team when they were exiting the airport.
words.solution: Exultant means triumphantly happy. Rejoicing, jubilant and elated are synonyms; disconsolate (very unhappy, beyond comfort) is the opposite.
Fabulous means extraordinary, wonderful, so its synonym is remarkable. Resourceful means good at finding ways, regrettable means unfortunate, and restful means calm.

words.sentence: Ram \(\underline{\text{failed}}\) initially but after a few years, he _________ in every field.
words.solution: The opposite of failed is succeeded, and "succeeded in every field" completes the contrast set up by "but".

words.sentence: The note drew attention to the \(\underline{\text{fallacious}}\) assumptions underlying the proposals.
words.solution: Fallacious means based on a mistaken belief - false or logically unsound. Its opposite is veracious, meaning truthful and accurate. Misleading and erroneous are synonyms of fallacious, while procedural relates to procedure and says nothing about truth or falsity. Note that veracious (truthful) is a different word from voracious (greedy).
A fallacy is a mistaken belief or an error in reasoning. Veracity (truthfulness) is its opposite; evidence and verify are unrelated.

words.sentence: This question gives a word followed by four choices. From the choices, select the most suitable synonym (word which means the same) for the main word and mark its number as the answer. FAMISHED
words.solution:
Famished means very hungry.
Hungry has the same meaning.
Agricultural (of farming), prestigious (having high standing) and feasible (possible) do not mean hungry.
So the answer is (B) Hungry.

words.sentence: His religious views are rather \(\underline{\text{fanatical}}\).
words.solution: Answer: C. Antonym of 'fanatical' (extreme, zealous) is 'moderate'. Bigoted, rabid and militant are synonyms, not opposites.

words.sentence: Keshav planned the event with \(\underline{\text{fastidious}}\) care.
words.solution: Answer: C. 'Fastidious' means very attentive to accuracy and detail; the nearest synonym is 'meticulous'.
Fatal means causing death, that is, deadly. Additional, easy and jovial (cheerful) are unrelated.
Fatigue means extreme tiredness. Vigour is its opposite, and mission and obese are unrelated.

words.sentence: Uninterrupted rain had \(\underline{\text{fatigued}}\) the commuters from the outskirts to the city and work suffered.
words.solution: Answer: D. 'Fatigued' means tired or exhausted; 'exhausted' is the nearest synonym.
Feeble means lacking strength, that is weak. Strong is its antonym, unheedful means careless, and baneful means harmful.
"Felicitous" means well chosen and apt, or pleasing and fortunate. "Fortunate", "happy" and "appropriate" are all close to it in meaning; "unfortunate" is the opposite.

words.sentence: My parents have a \(\underline{\text{fertile}}\) land in the backyard.
words.solution: Fertile land is productive; its opposite is barren land, which produces nothing. Scanty means insufficient, potent means powerful and timid means shy, none of which is the opposite of fertile.
Festivity means joyful celebration or merrymaking. Silence, argument and disappointment have nothing of that sense.

words.sentence: Recession \(\underline{\text{fettered}}\) the company from any further investments.
words.solution: "Fettered" means restrained or held back (a fetter is a chain on the feet); its opposite is "liberated", set free. "Concealed" means hidden, "valuable" means precious, and "depended" means relied on.

words.sentence: The long-standing \(\underline{\text{feud}}\) between the two villages was settled due to the intervention of the two chiefs.
words.solution: A feud is a prolonged bitter quarrel. Its opposite is harmony (peaceful agreement). Humility, honesty and humble are unrelated to conflict.

words.sentence: My first lecture in the classroom was a \(\underline{\text{fiasco}}\).
words.solution: 'Fiasco' means a complete failure; its antonym is 'success'. 'Disaster' is a synonym, 'joy' and 'fun' are unrelated. Matches option A: success.

words.sentence: The \(\underline{\text{fickle}}\) nature of humans is at times the cause of great innovations.
words.solution: 'Fickle' means changing frequently; the nearest synonym is 'vacillating' (indecisive, changing). Matches option A: vacillating.

words.sentence: Many of the incidents in the autobiography appear to be \(\underline{\text{fictitious}}\). Select the word which is opposite in meaning of the underlined.
words.solution:
'Fictitious' means made up, not real. Its opposite is 'genuine', which means real and authentic.
'Imaginary' is close in meaning to fictitious. 'Boring' and 'creative' are not opposites of it.
So the answer is (D) genuine.
Fierce means violent, intense or aggressive. Gentle is the opposite; fanatic and fraud are unrelated.
"Filthy" means very dirty. "Tidy" and "shiny" suggest the opposite, and "visual" means relating to sight.

words.sentence: He had a \(\underline{\text{fine}}\) ear for music.
words.solution: Fine ear means a delicate, sensitive ability to perceive; the antonym is coarse (lacking sensitivity). Matches option C: coarse.

words.sentence: The government's new policies will come into force from the next \(\underline{\text{fiscal}}\) year.
words.solution: Fiscal relates to government finances or revenue; financial is the closest synonym. Matches option C: financial.

words.sentence: I don't like to work with people who are not \(\underline{\text{flexible}}\).
words.solution: Flexible means able to adapt or bend; its opposite is rigid. Malleable and open-ended are close in meaning to flexible, and capable is unrelated.

words.sentence: The business \(\underline{\text{floundered}}\) during the pandemic.
words.solution: Answer: A. To 'flounder' is to struggle clumsily, be in serious difficulty. The nearest meaning is 'faced many problems'. 'Glided through'/'floated through'/'succeeded' are opposites.

words.sentence: They consider themselves as \(\underline{\text{foes}}\) from birth.
words.solution: Answer: C. 'Foes' means enemies. Its antonym is 'Friends'. (Soul mates is a distractor but 'Friends' is the direct opposite of foes/enemies.)

words.sentence: One should \(\underline{\text{follow}}\) the role models in life.
words.solution: To follow a role model is to copy or imitate them, which is to emulate. Admire and cherish are feelings, not actions of following, and reward does not fit.

To foment is to stir up or instigate (trouble, unrest). Its opposite is to keep in check or control, which "regulate" gives. Separation, remoteness and proximity are about distance and have no link to the word.

words.sentence: Her parents \(\underline{\text{forbade}}\) her to marry her lover.
words.solution: "Forbade" (past of forbid) means did not allow. The opposite is "allowed". Prevented, refused and declined are close in meaning to forbade.

words.sentence: We should follow patience and \(\underline{\text{forbearance}}\).
words.solution: Answer: C. Forbearance means patient self-control or restraint.
Forbid means to refuse to permit; its opposite is allow. Prohibit is a synonym, and call and forsake (abandon) are unrelated.
"Forbidden" means not allowed, so its opposite is "Allowed". "Banned" and "prevented" are close in meaning, and "protected" is unrelated.

To forgive is to give up resentment and feel goodwill towards someone who did wrong. To loathe is to feel intense hatred, the opposite attitude. Clear and unburden are close in sense to forgiving, and requite means to repay, which can be for good or for ill.
To forsake is to abandon or give up (forsake one's friends). Clutch is close to its opposite; accelerate and reveal are unrelated.

words.sentence: The parental support can \(\underline{\text{fortify}}\) a child's learning.
words.solution: 'Fortify' means to strengthen or reinforce. Its antonym is 'weaken'. Matches option A: weaken.

words.sentence: The emperor as a centralised entity indisputably went beyond regional conflicts and \(\underline{\text{fostered}}\) a certain mode of elite culture.
words.solution: Answer: C. To 'foster' is to encourage, nurture, promote. The opposite is 'suppressed' (held back, stifled). 'Cultivated', 'endorsed', 'incubated' all carry a promoting/nurturing sense.
Fragile means easily broken, delicate. Firm is nearly the opposite, and composed (calm) and fanatic (extreme in belief) are unrelated.

words.sentence: His \(\underline{\text{frail}}\) appearance was considered a merit.
words.solution: 'Frail' means weak or delicate; its antonym is 'sturdy' (strong and robust). Options A and B are synonyms of frail. Matches option C: sturdy.

words.sentence: Maria thinks the animals that live in \(\underline{\text{freedom}}\) have a sad look in their eyes.
words.solution: The opposite of living in "freedom" is living in "captivity" (confinement). "Liberty" is a synonym, "carefree" is an adjective of a related sense, and "surrendered" is a verb form, not the opposite noun.

**Note:** Both "summery" and "tropical" are opposite in meaning to "freezing"; "tropical", the hotter word, is the closer opposite.

"Freezing" means extremely cold. Its opposite is a word meaning very hot: "tropical" (very hot and humid, as in the tropics). "Summery" (warm, typical of summer) is also opposite in sense but milder. "Brisk" (cold and fresh, of weather) is close to "freezing", and "gnawing" means persistent and troubling.

words.sentence: He is not \(\underline{\text{friendly}}\) with him in the office.
words.solution: "Friendly" means kind and pleasant; its opposite is **hostile** (unfriendly, antagonistic). "Gregarious" (sociable) is close in meaning to friendly, "revel" means to enjoy oneself, and "intelligent" is unrelated.
"Frugal" means careful and sparing with money, so "thrifty". "Lavish", "extravagant" and "wasteful" all mean spending freely, the opposite.

words.sentence: Even though James won the election, he has not brought any of his campaign promises to \(\underline{\text{fruition}}\).
words.solution: "Fruition" means the realisation or fulfilment of a plan, so "bring promises to fruition" means to accomplish them. The meaning is "accomplishment".
Fulsome (as in fulsome praise) means excessive and flattering to the point of seeming insincere. Overdone, excessive and lavish are near-synonyms; sincere is the opposite.

words.sentence: The movie is about \(\underline{\text{fusion}}\) of old and contemporary ideas.
words.solution: Answer: C. 'Fusion' = merging/blending together. The opposite is 'separation'. 'Joining', 'bonding', 'blending' are synonyms.
"Futile" means producing no result, useless. Its opposite is "effective" (producing the intended result). "Useless", "pointless" and "vain" are synonyms of futile.

words.sentence: If you listen carefully you'll discover that the soundtrack is \(\underline{\text{fuzzy}}\) in places.
words.solution: Answer: C. Of a sound, fuzzy means indistinct or blurred, so clear is its opposite. Distorted and vague restate it.
To garnish is to decorate or embellish, especially food. Dwindle means diminish; blemish and tarnish mean spoil or stain.
Garrulous means excessively talkative, especially about trivial things. Reserved and silent are its opposites; listen is unrelated.

words.sentence: His thesis makes all \(\underline{\text{generic}}\) statements which have already been proved.
words.solution: Answer: C. 'Generic' means general or broad in scope; 'broad' is nearest. 'Specific' is the antonym.
"Generous" means willing to give freely. "Selfish" is its opposite. Magnanimous, altruistic and benevolent are all near synonyms.
Genial means friendly and cheerful in manner. Despondent is the opposite; optimistic and positive describe hopeful outlook, not a pleasant, cheerful manner.
Gentle means kind, mild and tender. Of the options only sympathetic (kind, caring) is close; fierce, ferocious and cruel are its opposites.
Genuine means real or authentic. Deceptive and fabricated are near-opposites; erroneous means wrong.

words.sentence: His \(\underline{\text{gibbous}}\) looks make him different from others.
words.solution: Answer: A. Gibbous means humped/convex/protuberant; hunched is nearest.

words.sentence: Suddenly, the sky was darkened by a \(\underline{\text{gigantic}}\) bird.
words.solution: The word 'gigantic' means extremely large; 'enormous' is the direct synonym. Matches option D: enormous.
"Glorify" means to praise highly or honour. Simplify (make simple), stupefy (stun) and strengthen (make strong) do not match.
Glory is great honour and fame. Its opposite is *shame* (disgrace). Honour is a near-synonym, delight means great pleasure, and gluttony means overeating.

words.sentence: A local court \(\underline{\text{granted}}\) bail to the criminal on Thursday.
words.solution: Granted bail means officially allowed or gave permission for bail; allowed is the closest in meaning. Matches option C: allowed.

words.sentence: These days there is a lot of \(\underline{\text{gratuitous}}\) violence on television.
words.solution: Answer: A. Gratuitous here means uncalled for or done without good reason, i.e. unjustified. Gratifying and grating are sound-alike distractors.
"Gregarious" means fond of company, so "sociable". "Quiet", "shy" and "reserved" describe someone who keeps to themselves, the opposite.

words.sentence: The university has constituted a \(\underline{\text{grievance}}\) redressal committee to look into the matter.
words.solution: The word 'grievance' means a formal complaint or cause for complaint; 'complaint' is the direct synonym. Matches option B: complaint.

"Grisly" means causing horror or disgust, gruesome: "a grisly murder". "Atrocious" (horrifyingly wicked or shocking) is the closest match. "Dire" means extremely serious or urgent ("dire need"), not horrifying; "pleasant" and "glorious" are opposite in tone.
Grotesque means comically or repulsively ugly or distorted. Comely (attractive) is its opposite; shameful and spontaneous are unrelated.
Grow means to increase in size; shrink means to become smaller. Crimp (to press into folds), plant and alter are not opposites.

words.sentence: His mother never held a **grudge** against his father.
words.solution: The sheet prints the whole sentence in bold, so no single word stands out; the word the options answer is "grudge" (lasting ill will or resentment). Its opposite is benevolence (goodwill, kindness). Malevolence and rancour mean much the same as grudge, and revulsion is disgust.

words.sentence: These were based primarily in Himachal Pradesh, where the treks were as \(\underline{\text{gruelling}}\) as the terrain.
words.solution: 'Gruelling' means extremely tiring and demanding; the nearest synonym is 'rigorous'. 'Egregious' means shockingly bad, which is unrelated. Matches option A: rigorous.
Grumpy means bad-tempered and easily annoyed, which is irritable. Friendly, polite and calm are near-opposites.
Gullibility is the tendency to believe things too easily. Its opposite is skepticism, a doubting attitude. Naivety, innocence and trust are close in meaning to gullibility.

words.sentence: He is too \(\underline{\text{gullible}}\) to believe manipulated versions of the happening.
words.solution:
Gullible means too ready to believe, which is the meaning of naive.
Unusual, gusty and equipoised do not match.
So the answer is (D) naive.
"Habitual" means done constantly or as a regular habit, so the closest option is "continuous". "Considerate" means thoughtful of others, "diverse" means varied, and "pertinent" means relevant.

words.sentence: He worked alone as he did not want anyone to \(\underline{\text{hamper}}\) his project.
words.solution: "Hamper" means to hinder or obstruct; its opposite is **help**. "Impede" is a synonym of hamper, and "care" and "finish" are not opposites.
Haphazard means lacking order or plan, done at random. Organized, intentional and planned are its opposites.
Hapless means unlucky or unfortunate (hap = luck, so "without luck"). Happy and fortunate are its opposites, and distasteful means unpleasant.

words.sentence: I was \(\underline{\text{happy}}\) to know that Sheila passed her final exams.
words.solution: The opposite of happy is sad. Upbeat and joyful are synonyms, and excited is close in feeling.

words.sentence: We’d better watch our step and not give him any excuse to **harass** us further.
words.solution: The sheet prints the whole sentence in bold, so no single word stands out; the only word the options can match is "harass" (to pressure or torment repeatedly). Intimidate (frighten, threaten) is the closest. Soothe is nearly opposite; betray and relish are unrelated.

words.sentence: He is considered the \(\underline{\text{harbinger}}\).
words.solution: Answer: B. A harbinger is a forerunner that announces or signals what is to come — an advance messenger.

words.sentence: The effort was to \(\underline{\text{harness}}\) the power of nature.
words.solution: 'Harness' means to control and make use of (natural resources); the nearest synonym here is 'control'. Matches option D: control.

words.sentence: He gave a \(\underline{\text{haughty}}\) consent without honouring him with a single word.
words.solution: "Haughty" means arrogant and proud, so its opposite is "Modest" (humble). "Proud" is a synonym, and "indifferent" and "happy" are not opposites.

words.sentence: The truck was carrying a \(\underline{\text{heavy}}\) load .
words.solution: The opposite of a heavy load is a light load. Big, massive and large are close in meaning to heavy.

words.sentence: Religious fundamentalists often consider the followers of other religions to be \(\underline{\text{heretics}}\).
words.solution: Answer: B. A 'heretic' holds opinions contrary to accepted doctrine; its antonym is 'believer' (one who conforms to the faith). Dissenter, renegade and apostate are synonyms of heretic.

words.sentence: Their new colour scheme is \(\underline{\text{hideous}}\).
words.solution: The concept is antonym identification: 'hideous' means extremely ugly/revolting. 'Beautiful' is its direct antonym. Options A, C, D are synonyms. Matches option B: beautiful.

words.sentence: This library building is very \(\underline{\text{high}}\) and has 25 floors.
words.solution: The opposite of high is low. Elevated is a synonym; hale and sturdy mean healthy or strong.

words.sentence: The film I saw was \(\underline{\text{hilarious}}\).
words.solution: Answer: A. 'Hilarious' means extremely funny. 'Uproarious' and 'jovial' are synonyms. Both 'tragic' and 'serious' are opposites of 'funny', so two options are defensible. The keyed answer is 'tragic': a film is the subject, and a tragic film (one that ends in suffering) is the full opposite of a hilarious one, while 'serious' only means not joking.
To hinder is to obstruct or make difficult; to facilitate is to make easier. Block is a synonym; praise and joy are unrelated.

words.sentence: The big tree \(\underline{\text{hindered}}\) access of sunlight into the house.
words.solution: Answer: A. Hindered = obstructed/impeded. Facilitated is the opposite.

words.sentence: The \(\underline{\text{Holocaust}}\) was experienced by millions.
words.solution: 'Holocaust' refers to destruction or slaughter on a mass scale; 'destruction' is the nearest synonym. Matches option B: destruction.

words.sentence: He was the most \(\underline{\text{honest}}\) and good-hearted man that she had ever met.
words.solution: Honest means truthful and genuine, which is sincere. Deceptive and fake are opposites; biased is unrelated.

words.sentence: He was appointed as the \(\underline{\text{honorary}}\) member of the team.
words.solution: 'Honorary' means holding a position without being paid; the nearest synonym is 'unpaid'. Matches option D: unpaid.

words.sentence: The magician \(\underline{\text{hoodwinked}}\) the children.
words.solution: Answer: C. To hoodwink is to deceive, and to disabuse is to free someone from a mistaken belief, which is its opposite. Cheated and fooled are synonyms, and unhooked plays on the shape of the word.

words.sentence: The local people are \(\underline{\text{hospitable}}\) to strangers.
words.solution: Answer: D. 'Hospitable' = friendly and welcoming. 'Cordial' (warm, friendly) is the nearest synonym. 'Surly', 'distant', 'frosty' are antonyms.
Hostile means unfriendly or antagonistic, so its opposite is friendly.

words.sentence: He has deeper \(\underline{\text{hostility}}\) towards Mohan.
words.solution: The word 'hostility' means unfriendly or aggressive feelings; its antonym is 'friendship' — a state of mutual goodwill. Matches option D: friendship.

words.sentence: Coffee was too \(\underline{\text{hot}}\); it burnt my tongue.
words.solution: Hot is opposed by frigid (very cold). Scorching is a synonym, balmy means pleasantly warm, and subtle is unrelated.

words.sentence: The oceans carry a \(\underline{\text{huge}}\) amount of heat from the tropics to the high latitudes.
words.solution: The antonym of 'huge' (very large) is 'tiny' (very small). Matches option C: tiny.

words.sentence: The \(\underline{\text{hypothesis}}\) that the police believed in led to a lot of chaos.
words.solution: A "hypothesis" is a supposition or proposed explanation not yet proved, which is a "speculation". A "breakthrough" is a sudden important discovery, "trepidation" is fear, and an "encounter" is a meeting.

words.sentence: How \(\underline{\text{hysterical}}\) he is!
words.solution: Answer: A. 'Hysterical' (wildly emotional, out of control) is nearest to 'berserk'. Inconsistent/duplicitous/insincere relate to character, not frenzied emotion.

words.sentence: The novel presents an \(\underline{\text{idealistic}}\) view of the ongoing political reform.
words.solution: Idealistic means judging things by an ideal standard rather than by practical reality. Its opposite is pragmatic - dealing with matters in a practical, realistic way. Visionary, utopian and romantic all belong to the same family of meaning as idealistic.

words.sentence: He was just \(\underline{\text{idle}}\) by temperament.
words.solution: 'Idle' means avoiding work; lazy. Its antonym is industrious (hardworking). Matches option C: industrious.
"Ignominy" means public shame or disgrace. "Respect", "fame" and "honor" are all opposite in sense.
To illuminate is to light up, and figuratively to make clear or explain (the example illuminated the rule). Darken and hide are its opposites; destroy is unrelated.

An "imbroglio" is a confused, complicated or embarrassing situation, often a bitter misunderstanding or dispute. Its opposite among the options is "agreement". "Entanglement", "complication" and "dispute" are close in meaning.

words.sentence: The city has **immense** coal piers.
words.solution: The word asked about is "immense", which means extremely large: huge. Diminutive and trifling mean small or unimportant, the opposite.
To immerse is to dip into a liquid or, figuratively, to involve oneself deeply in something (immersed in work). Emerge and uncover are nearer its opposite; distant is unrelated.

words.sentence: She believed that it was \(\underline{\text{imminent}}\) that he would be chosen as the leader of the group.
words.solution: 'Imminent' means about to happen very soon; the closest in meaning is 'inevitable' (certain to happen). Matches option D: inevitable.

To be "immune" is to be resistant to (unaffected by) a disease or influence: "immune to criticism" means resistant to it. "Safe" is close but only describes being out of danger, not the resisting itself; "asleep" and "variable" are unrelated.
Impecunious means having little or no money. Insolvent, indigent and penniless are near-synonyms; wealthy is the opposite.

words.sentence: Learning of foreign language should not \(\underline{\text{impede}}\) one's mother tongue learning.
words.solution: Answer: C. Impede means to obstruct or hinder. 'Hinder' is the direct synonym; 'facilitate' is the opposite.
Implacable means unable to be appeased or moved (an implacable enemy), so its synonym is unyielding. Soft, flexible and gentle are close to its opposite.

words.sentence: He tried to avoid saying something that would \(\underline{\text{implicate}}\) him further.
words.solution: Answer: B. To implicate = to show/suggest someone is involved in a crime or wrongdoing. Nearest synonym is incriminate.

words.sentence: All the developments that took place in the 20th century have had \(\underline{\text{implications}}\) for the next century.
words.solution: Answer: A. 'Implications' here means likely consequences or effects. 'Consequences' is nearest in meaning.
"Important" means of great value or consequence; "trivial" means of little value or importance. "Significant" is a synonym; "productive" and "recurring" are unrelated.

words.sentence: The properties of the family have been \(\underline{\text{impounded}}\) by the order of the court.
words.solution: Answer: A. To 'impound' (esp. by a court) means to seize/take legal possession of property. 'Confiscated' is nearest in meaning.

words.sentence: The controversial policy received the committee's \(\underline{\text{imprimatur}}\).
words.solution: An imprimatur is an official licence or sanction - originally the Church's permission to print a book - and so means approval. An appraisal is only an assessment, which is not the same as giving sanction to something.

words.sentence: Weather conditions have been \(\underline{\text{improving}}\) over the past few days.
words.solution: Improving means becoming better over time; 'becoming better' is the most direct synonym. Matches option C: becoming better.

words.sentence: The officer in charge of the operations has been \(\underline{\text{impugned}}\) for the excesses.
words.solution: Answer: C. To impugn someone is to call their conduct into question or attack it as wrong. An officer impugned for excesses has been challenged over them, so 'Challenged' is nearest in meaning. 'Expelled' goes too far: being questioned is not the same as being thrown out. 'Rewarded' and 'Given allowance' point the opposite way.

words.sentence: The entry was carried out \(\underline{\text{inadvertently}}\).
words.solution: Answer: A. 'Inadvertently' means unintentionally/accidentally. Its antonym is 'Purposely' (deliberately). 'Purposively' is a near-synonym distractor; 'Purposely' is the standard antonym of inadvertently.
Incandescent means glowing brightly with heat or light. Resplendent, glistening and fulgent all describe brightness; dusky (dim, darkish) is the opposite.

words.sentence: His \(\underline{\text{incendiary}}\) remarks precipitated disaffection among the group.
words.solution: Answer: D. Incendiary remarks are those calculated to inflame, i.e. provocative. Insensitive is weaker and does not carry the sense of stirring up trouble.
Incessant means continuing without a pause. Constant, ceaseless and perpetual are synonyms; intermittent (stopping and starting at intervals) is the opposite.

words.sentence: The government is proposing to \(\underline{\text{incinerate}}\) cattle carcasses at many sites, some of which are in populated areas.
words.solution: To "incinerate" is to burn something completely; to "extinguish" is to put out a fire. "Oxidise", "blaze" and "combust" all go with burning.
Incipient means in an initial stage, just beginning. Nascent, developing and budding are near-synonyms; advanced (at a late or developed stage) is the opposite.

words.sentence: He wrote an \(\underline{\text{incisive}}\) article on corruption in politics.
words.solution: The key concept is antonym identification. 'Incisive' means intelligently analytical and clear; its antonym is 'vague' (not clearly expressed). Matches option A: vague.

words.sentence: People have been advised not to venture into sea as the weather is likely to be \(\underline{\text{inclement}}\)
words.solution: Inclement = stormy/harsh weather; nearest synonym is squally. Matches option A.

Incompetent means lacking the skill to do something well. Dexterous means skilful, especially with the hands, so it is the opposite. Forlorn, desperate and hopeless describe states of despair, not ability.

words.sentence: Such traditional methods seem \(\underline{\text{incongruous}}\) in our technical age.
words.solution: Answer: D. 'Incongruous' = out of place, not in harmony, unsuitable. 'Inappropriate' is the nearest synonym among the options.

words.sentence: The budget \(\underline{\text{incorporated}}\) a number of tax reforms which included higher taxes for the very rich.
words.solution: Answer: B. 'Incorporated' means included or integrated into a whole; 'integrated' is nearest.

Incorrigible means not able to be corrected or reformed. Chronic, deep-rooted and habitual are close in sense (a habit too fixed to change). Reclaimable, able to be reformed or recovered, is the opposite.
Incredible means impossible or hard to believe, that is unbelievable. Realistic and reasonable are near-opposites; unachievable means impossible to do, not to believe.

words.sentence: We must remember that what we teach our children is what we \(\underline{\text{inculcate}}\) in them.
words.solution: To inculcate is to fix an idea or habit in someone's mind by repeated teaching, which is to instil it. "Instil in them" also keeps the sentence's preposition. Inspire does not take "in them" this way, and endanger and import do not fit the meaning.

words.sentence: The brave soldiers left an \(\underline{\text{indelible}}\) impression on the people of the land.
words.solution: 'Indelible' means permanent, unable to be removed. Matches option A: permanent.

"Indigenous" means native to a place, originating there. Its synonym is **aboriginal** (inhabiting a land from the earliest times). "Artificial" (man-made), "tangible" (able to be touched) and "literary" (relating to literature) do not mean this.
"Indigent" means very poor and needy, so "impoverished" is the synonym. "Affluent" (wealthy) is its opposite, "bust" is slang for broken or bankrupt, and "low" is too general.

words.sentence: The \(\underline{\text{indignant}}\) attitude of the speaker made the groups unhappy.
words.solution: Answer: A. 'Indignant' means angry/resentful at something unjust; 'resentful' is nearest in meaning.

words.sentence: The police fired \(\underline{\text{indiscriminately}}\) at the crowd, killing many innocent women and children.
words.solution: 'Indiscriminately' means without making a distinction; 'without distinguishing' captures this directly. 'Foolishly' implies poor judgement (not the same), 'continuously' refers to manner not selectivity. Matches option B: without distinguishing.

words.sentence: Sachin Tendulkar was an \(\underline{\text{indispensable}}\) member of the Indian cricket team in his days.
words.solution: Indispensable means absolutely necessary, that is, essential. Optional is its opposite.

words.sentence: The growth and development of the peasant movement was \(\underline{\text{indissolubly}}\) linked with the national struggle for freedom.
words.solution: Indissolubly means in a way that cannot be separated; firmly is the closest in meaning. Matches option A: firmly.

words.sentence: I abandoned the task due to \(\underline{\text{indolence}}.\)
words.solution: 'Indolence' means habitual laziness or avoidance of work. Matches option B: laziness.
Indolent means lazy, wanting to avoid activity. Lazy and sluggish are synonyms; active is the opposite. Unskilled is unrelated.

words.sentence: The newly appointed secretary is \(\underline{\text{industrious}}\).
words.solution: Answer: A. 'Industrious' means hard-working/diligent; 'diligent' is nearest in meaning.

words.sentence: He was upbraided for appearing in court in a state of \(\underline{\text{inebriation}}\).
words.solution: 'Inebriation' means the state of being drunk. Common error is choosing 'confabulation' (fabricating memories). The nearest synonym is 'intoxication'. Matches option B: intoxication.

words.sentence: A good work place shall not encourage \(\underline{\text{ineptitude}}\) even in a hidden manner.
words.solution: Answer: A. Ineptitude means lack of skill or competence; 'incompetence' is the direct synonym.

words.sentence: According to G B Shaw, men have become \(\underline{\text{inert}}\). Therefore, life force has chosen women to perform its functions.
words.solution: Answer: A. Antonym of 'inert' (inactive, motionless) is 'lively' (active, energetic). Quiescent, dormant and apathetic are synonyms of inert.

words.sentence: Everyone has to fight the \(\underline{\text{inertia}}\) in the system.
words.solution: Answer: C. 'Inertia' means inactivity or sluggishness; its opposite is 'activity'. The other options are synonyms.
Inevitable means certain to happen, unavoidable, so its antonym is avoidable. Inexorable is a near-synonym; confident and clear are unrelated.

words.sentence: He was rebuked for his \(\underline{\text{infraction}}\) of the discipline.
words.solution: Answer: B. 'Infraction' means a violation/breach of a rule. The opposite is 'observance' (compliance with a rule). 'Transgression' and 'breach' are synonyms; 'acceptance' is weaker than observance but observance is the precise antonym of a rule-violation.

words.sentence: It is \(\underline{\text{ingenuous}}\) to suppose that money did not play a part in his decision.
words.solution: Answer: A. Ingenuous means innocent, unsuspecting, naive (not to be confused with ingenious). Nearest meaning is naive.

words.sentence: The \(\underline{\text{inherent}}\) danger in the problem is that it would lead to many more problems.
words.solution: Answer: D. 'Inherent' means existing as a natural, built-in part; 'inbuilt' is the closest synonym.

words.sentence: He is often accused of being \(\underline{\text{iniquitous}}\) in his conduct.
words.solution: Answer: C. 'Iniquitous' means grossly unfair, wicked, immoral. Its antonym is 'virtuous' (morally good). Execrable and revolting are synonyms; preposterous (absurd) is unrelated.

words.sentence: He \(\underline{\text{initiated}}\) the dialogue.
words.solution: Answer: C. Initiated = began/started.
"Injustice" is unfair treatment; "Discrimination" (treating people unfairly) is the closest. "Equality" is nearer an opposite, and "complacency" and "demand" are unrelated.
Innate means inborn, present from birth. Its opposite is learned (acquired through experience). Natural is a synonym; aquatic and replete are unrelated.
Innocent means not guilty of a crime or wrongdoing, so its opposite is guilty. Mischievous (playfully naughty) is only loosely opposed, righteous is close to innocent, and unfair is unrelated.
Innocuous means harmless, not likely to cause injury or offence. Its opposite is harmful. "Harmless", "benign" and "safe" are synonyms.
An innuendo is an indirect, usually unflattering hint or remark, which is an insinuation. Crude, prose and ragged are unrelated.

words.sentence: Drinking \(\underline{\text{inordinate}}\) amount of liquor is not good for health.
words.solution: 'Inordinate' means unusually or disproportionately large; excessive. 'Exorbitant' is the closest synonym meaning unreasonably large. Matches option B: exorbitant.

words.sentence: If you want to be a good detective, it helps to have an \(\underline{\text{inquisitive}}\) nature.
words.solution: Inquisitive means eager to know or curious. Disinterested (here, not interested) is the opposite. Intrusive is close in meaning, and comprehensive and itemised are unrelated.

words.sentence: In the question, four alternatives are given for the underlined word in the sentence. Choose the alternative which best expresses the opposite meaning of the word. It was as if the newer hybrids had an \(\underline{\text{insatiable}}\) appetite for chemicals.
words.solution: Insatiable means impossible to satisfy, so its opposite is satisfiable. Urgent and pressing are close to its sense of a demanding need; curbed means restrained, which describes an action, not the appetite's capacity to be satisfied.

words.sentence: The \(\underline{\text{inscrutability}}\) surrounding the incident remains unresolved until the end of the movie
words.solution: Inscrutability = the quality of being impossible to understand; nearest synonym is mystery. Matches option D.
To insert is to put something in; to remove is to take it out. Inject is close to a synonym.

words.sentence: His intentions are \(\underline{\text{insidious}}.\)
words.solution: 'Insidious' means proceeding in a subtle, treacherous way; the closest synonym is 'deceitful'. Matches option C: deceitful.
"Insipid" means lacking flavour, or dull and uninteresting, so "tasteless" is the synonym. "Dismal" means gloomy, "obscure" means unclear or little known, and "idle" means inactive.

words.sentence: The \(\underline{\text{insolent}}\) nature of the speaker had provoked the members of the house and this led to pandemonium.
words.solution: Answer: A. 'Insolent' means rude/disrespectful. Its antonym is 'Respectful'. 'Impudent' is a synonym; 'Autocratic' and 'Thought provoking' are unrelated.

words.sentence: The manager always provides \(\underline{\text{instantaneous}}\) replies to all queries.
words.solution: 'Instantaneous' means happening instantly. The nearest synonym is 'immediate'. Matches option A: immediate.

words.sentence: The Professor has been able to \(\underline{\text{instil}}\) confidence in her students
words.solution: Instil = to gradually introduce/infuse; nearest synonym is inculcate (to teach by repetition). Matches option A.

words.sentence: His \(\underline{\text{integrity}}\) is noticed.
words.solution: 'Integrity' means moral uprightness; its antonym is 'dishonesty'. Matches option D: dishonesty.
Intelligible means able to be understood. Incoherent (unclear, impossible to follow) is the opposite; the other words are unrelated.

words.sentence: An \(\underline{\text{intense}}\) wish to learn something keeps the nerves active.
words.solution: Intense means very strong or powerful. Lazy and half-hearted are opposites; fixed does not mean strong.
Intentional means done on purpose, deliberately; unplanned (accidental) is its opposite. Cordial and amiable mean friendly, and inanimate means lifeless.

words.sentence: The case of Vanuatu in 2020 is a clear example of the constant and complex challenges faced by SIDS. It shows how SIDS are dealing with multiple crises at the same time and how COVID-19 has particularly exposed SIDS’ extreme and \(\underline{\text{interlinked}}\) vulnerabilities.
words.solution: Interlinked means joined or connected with one another. Interlaced (woven together, intertwined) has the same meaning. Continuous, severe and free do not mean connected.
To "interpret" is to explain the meaning of something, that is, to clarify it. "Complicate" is nearly its opposite, and "cleanse" and "celebrate" are unrelated.

words.sentence: The Professor assured us that her class lectures would be \(\underline{\text{interspersed}}\) with practical demonstrations.
words.solution: Answer: C. Interspersed means scattered/mixed among other things — nearest in meaning to combined.
"Intimate" means closely acquainted or very personal. Its opposite is "distant". "Close", "familiar" and "personal" are near synonyms.

words.sentence: The police officer tried to \(\underline{\text{intimidate}}\) the witness but in vain.
words.solution: 'Intimidate' means to frighten or overawe someone. The officer tried to frighten the witness. Matches option C: frighten.

words.sentence: He has been facing a kind of \(\underline{\text{intimidation}}\) by his friends for last two years.
words.solution: Answer: D. 'Intimidation' means threatening/coercion. Its antonym is 'Support' (helping, encouraging). 'Wiles', 'Conviction', 'Persuasion' do not reverse the threatening sense.

"Intransigence" is a refusal to change one's views or agree. Its opposite is "compromise", a willingness to meet others halfway. "Obstinacy", "defiance" and "rigidity" are close in meaning to intransigence.
Intransigent means refusing to change one's views or to agree; unwilling to compromise. Stubborn matches. Willing, compliant and submissive are close to its opposite.
Intriguing means arousing curiosity or interest, so its synonym is interesting. Ravishing and stunning describe beauty; glorifying means praising.

words.sentence: Respect for other human beings is \(\underline{\text{intrinsic}}\) to the teachings of all religions.
words.solution: 'Intrinsic' means belonging naturally, essentially; 'inherent' is the closest synonym. Matches option C: inherent.
Invective is abusive, highly critical language; a tirade is a long angry speech of criticism. Eulogy, compliment and praise are the opposite.

words.sentence: American Independence was a great blow to the \(\underline{\text{invincible}}\) image of Great Britain.
words.solution: Answer: A. 'Invincible' means unconquerable, unbeatable. Its opposite is 'vulnerable' (open to attack/defeat). 'Impregnable', 'unbeatable', 'insurmountable' are synonyms.

words.sentence: The scholar quoted \(\underline{\text{irrefutable}}\) evidence for her thesis.
words.solution: 'Irrefutable' means impossible to deny or disprove; its antonym is 'questionable' (open to doubt). Options A, B, C are synonyms or near-synonyms. Matches option D: questionable.

Irrepressible means impossible to hold back or restrain (irrepressible laughter, an irrepressible spirit), so its synonym is uncontrollable. Forgettable, unbearable and avoidable do not carry that sense.

words.sentence: He is forced to lead an \(\underline{\text{itinerant}}\) life.
words.solution: Answer: C. 'Itinerant' = travelling from place to place, wandering. The opposite is 'settled'. 'Vagrant', 'roving', 'nomadic' are synonyms.

words.sentence: The \(\underline{\text{itinerary}}\) of the group's visit to the hills was given to everyone.
words.solution: 'Itinerary' means a planned route or schedule of a journey. The nearest synonym is 'schedule'. Matches option C: schedule.

Jargon is special words used by a particular group that outsiders find hard to understand. Slang (informal words of a particular group) is the closest. Verboseness is wordiness, formality and eloquence are unrelated.

words.sentence: We are planning a \(\underline{\text{jaunt}}\) for a while during the winter.
words.solution: Answer: C. A jaunt is a short trip or excursion — nearest to expedition.

words.sentence: In Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice, Shylock's connivance aimed to \(\underline{\text{jeopardise}}\) Antonio's life.
words.solution: To jeopardise is to put in danger, so its opposite is to safeguard (protect). Risk and peril are close in meaning to jeopardise, and a jape is a joke.

words.sentence: The teammates made several \(\underline{\text{jibes}}\) at the opponent team members during the interview.
words.solution:
**Note:** None of the options is a true antonym of "jibes". The answer shown follows SSC's answer key.

A jibe is an insulting or mocking remark. Mockery (D) is a synonym. None of the other options is a clean opposite such as 'praise' or 'compliment'. SSC's key gives B (Contradict); consolation (C), words of comfort, is the nearest opposite in meaning.
Jovial means cheerful and friendly. Miserable and solemnity are near opposites, and profane means disrespectful of sacred things.

words.sentence: How can you be so \(\underline{\text{joyless}}\) on hearing the news?
words.solution: Joyless means without joy, unhappy. The opposite state of mind is *blissful* (full of joy, extremely happy). Beaming describes a broad smile, an outward look rather than the state itself; rapt means completely absorbed and dubious means doubtful.

words.sentence: Instead of becoming \(\underline{\text{joyous}}\) to hear the breaking news, she became _________ .
words.solution: "Instead of" sets up a contrast with joyous, so the blank needs its opposite: melancholic (sad). Ecstatic and exuberant are synonyms of joyous; vengeful is unrelated.
Jubilant means full of joy and triumph. Its opposite is melancholic (sad, gloomy). Gay (in its old sense, cheerful) is a synonym; indifferent and thoughtful are unrelated.

words.sentence: The choice was **judicious** as further events proved.
words.solution: Judicious means showing good judgement, sensible and wise, which is prudent. Hasty, ridiculous and silly all point the other way.

words.sentence: We should plan our actions \(\underline{\text{judiciously}}\) before going to war.
words.solution: Judiciously means with good judgement and sense. The option opposite in meaning is irrational (without reason or sound judgement). Irrelevant (not connected), irreverent (disrespectful) and irritatingly (annoyingly) are not opposites of sound judgement.
Juvenile means young, or immature and childish in behaviour. Adult and mature are its opposites, and wise is unrelated.
Kilter means good working order or balance, as in "out of kilter". Anarchy, shambles and disrepair are all states of disorder.
Labour is hard work, and toil means hard, continuous work. Relaxation and dalliance (idle time-wasting) are close to the opposite; mesh is a net-like material.
Lachrymose means tearful or given to weeping. Tearful, mournful and weepy are near-synonyms; jovial (cheerful, good-humoured) is the opposite.
"Laconic" means using very few words, so "concise". "Wordy", "talkative" and "verbose" all mean using many words, the opposite.
To lament is to mourn or express grief; the opposite is to celebrate. Deplore, decry and regret all express disapproval or sorrow, so they lie on the same side as lament.

words.sentence: Her act was considered as most \(\underline{\text{lamentable}}\).
words.solution: Answer: D. Lamentable means regrettable/deplorable.

words.sentence: She was \(\underline{\text{lamenting}}\) her destiny.
words.solution: Lamenting means expressing grief or sorrow; 'bemoaning' is the exact synonym. Matches option B: bemoaning.
"Languid" means slow and lacking energy; its opposite is "energetic". "Lazy" is close to a synonym, and "exceptional" and "loyal" are unrelated.

words.sentence: An elephant is a \(\underline{\text{large}}\) mammal.
words.solution: The opposite of large is tiny. Bumper and gigantic mean large, and heroic is unrelated.
Lassitude is physical or mental weariness. Exhaustion, apathy and lethargy are near-synonyms; vigor (energy, vitality) is the opposite.
Laudable means deserving praise. Commendable is a synonym; deplorable (deserving strong condemnation) is the opposite.

words.sentence: He spends his money \(\underline{\text{lavishly}}\).
words.solution: Lavishly means in a very generous or extravagant manner; generously is the closest synonym. Matches option B: generously.

words.sentence: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. Gentlemen always go for a \(\underline{\text{lawful}}\) approach, but rouges choose ______ ways to solve problems.
words.solution: "Lawful" means permitted by law; its opposite is "illicit" (forbidden by law). "Legitimate" and "legal" are synonyms of "lawful", and "sophisticated" is unrelated.

words.sentence: We went to a \(\underline{\text{legitimate}}\) Mexican restaurant for my birthday, where they served cuisine like you would find in Mexico.
words.solution: Here legitimate means authentic, real ("cuisine like you would find in Mexico"), so genuine. Fictitious and falsified are opposites.

words.sentence: One of Ram's \(\underline{\text{leisure}}\) activities is tennis.
words.solution: Leisure activities are those done in free time for enjoyment, that is recreation. Languish means to weaken or decline, and main and lead do not mean free time.

words.sentence: He walked \(\underline{\text{leisurely}}\) towards the entrance.
words.solution: "Leisurely" means in an unhurried way, that is, without haste. "Hastily" is the opposite.
"Lenient" means mild or tolerant in punishing or judging. Its opposite is "strict". "Kind" is close to lenient, while "rude" and "rowdy" describe bad manners and noisy behaviour.

words.sentence: We usually had ____________ visitors dropping by, but now we have very \(\underline{\text{less}}\) visitors.
words.solution: The blank needs the opposite of "less" (few), describing a large number of visitors. Umpteen means very many. Insufficient, a handful of and slighter all point to a small amount.
Lethargic means sluggish and lacking energy. The opposite is active. Languid is a synonym.

words.sentence: There is no \(\underline{\text{likeness}}\) between him and his brother.
words.solution: Likeness means resemblance or similarity; the antonym is dissimilarity. Matches option C: dissimilarity.

words.sentence: The company was \(\underline{\text{liquidated}}\) within five years.
words.solution: Liquidated means dissolved or wound up (typically due to failure); the antonym is flourishing (thriving). Matches option C: flourishing.

words.sentence: He found the musical rendition by the septuagenarian maestro to be \(\underline{\text{listless}}\).
words.solution: 'Listless' means lacking energy or enthusiasm; its antonym is 'scintillating' (brilliantly lively). Matches option D: scintillating.

words.sentence: Those streets are very \(\underline{\text{lonely}}\).
words.solution: Lonely streets are deserted, with few people. The opposite is crowded. Isolated, empty and remote are close in meaning to lonely.

words.sentence: His opinion is \(\underline{\text{lopsided}}\).
words.solution: 'Lopsided' means uneven or with one side bigger than the other; its antonym is 'balanced' (equal and even on all sides). Matches option D: balanced.
Loving means showing love or warmth, the same as affectionate. Offish (distant, aloof) is nearly the opposite; rejuvenate and subordinate are unrelated.

words.sentence: He is essentially a \(\underline{\text{lowbrow}}\) person.
words.solution: 'Lowbrow' means lacking in cultural refinement or sophistication; 'coarse' is the closest synonym meaning crude or lacking in refinement. Matches option A: coarse.

words.sentence: Lucy presented a \(\underline{\text{lucid}}\) account of her achievements before the committee.
words.solution: Lucid means clear and easy to understand. Ambiguous (open to more than one meaning, unclear) is the opposite. Orderly, intelligible and transparent are close to its meaning.

words.sentence: \(\underline{\text{Lucidity}}\) is a desired quality in effective communication.
words.solution: 'Lucidity' means clearness of expression; its antonym is 'Ambiguity' (uncertainty of meaning). Option A is a synonym. Matches option D: Ambiguity.
Lugubrious means looking or sounding sad and dismal. Mournful, gloomy and sorrowful are synonyms; joyous is the opposite.
Luminous means full of or giving off light, bright. Radiant means the same. Dull and dim are its opposites, and opaque means not letting light through.

words.sentence: It is sheer \(\underline{\text{lunacy}}\) to drive a car in this frosty weather.
words.solution: 'Lunacy' means extreme foolishness or mental illness. 'Insanity' is its direct synonym. Matches option C: insanity.
"Magnanimous" means big-hearted and generous, especially towards a rival or someone less powerful. "Mean", "covetous" (greedy for what others have) and "petty" are its opposites.
"Magnificent" means impressively beautiful or grand; its synonym is **splendid**. "Humble" and "modest" are nearly opposite, and "regular" means ordinary.

words.sentence: John is a \(\underline{\text{magniloquent}}\) person.
words.solution: Answer: D. Magniloquent (using high-flown, bombastic language) is opposite to terse (concise/brief). Pompous/turgid/lofty are synonyms.

words.sentence: This is his \(\underline{\text{maiden}}\) appearance on the screen.
words.solution: 'Maiden' means first or earliest. His maiden appearance means his first appearance. Matches option A: first.
"Maladroit" means clumsy or unskilful (mal, badly + adroit, skilful). Its opposite is "skillful". "Clumsy", "awkward" and "inept" are synonyms.

words.sentence: He is a \(\underline{\text{maleficent}}\) person.
words.solution: 'Maleficent' means causing harm or destruction; 'cunning' is the nearest available option implying harmful craftiness. Common student error: confusing maleficent with 'criminal'. Matches option B: cunning.

words.sentence: His \(\underline{\text{malicious}}\) intentions were aborted.
words.solution: Answer: C. 'Malicious' = intending to do harm, spiteful. The opposite is 'benevolent' (kindly, well-meaning). 'Pernicious', 'spiteful', 'vindictive' are synonyms.

words.sentence: Ravi told his friend that he had no intention to \(\underline{\text{malign}}\) him.
words.solution: 'Malign' means to speak about someone in a spitefully critical manner (i.e., to slander). The closest synonym is 'slander'. Matches option B: slander.

words.sentence: Many metals are \(\underline{\text{malleable}}\) in nature and property.
words.solution: 'Malleable' means easily shaped or hammered without breaking; the antonym is 'hard' (resistant to deformation). Matches option A: hard.

words.sentence: Cleaning this mess is a \(\underline{\text{mammoth}}\) task
words.solution: Synonym of 'mammoth' (extremely large) is 'huge'. Matches option A: huge.

words.sentence: He had not completed the \(\underline{\text{mandatory}}\) training for his promotion to the level of senior manager.
words.solution: Answer: B. Mandatory means required by rule, i.e. compulsory. Recommendatory is its direct contrast, being advisory rather than required.

words.sentence: She deftly \(\underline{\text{masked}}\) her feelings.
words.solution: Answer: A. To mask one's feelings is to conceal/hide them. "Hid" is the direct synonym. "Obscured" can mean to make unclear but "hid" is the nearest in meaning to mask (to cover/conceal). "Flaunted" is opposite.

words.sentence: The Industrial Revolution saw a \(\underline{\text{massive}}\) rise in the population of Europe.
words.solution: 'Massive' means very large or great in scale; its closest synonym is 'enormous'. Options B/C/D carry different meanings (wrong, dangerous, risky). Matches option A: enormous.
Matching means corresponding to or being like something else, so resembling is the synonym. Distinguishing is nearly the opposite; appointing and adoring are unrelated.
Material means physical, made of matter. Its opposite is abstract (existing only as an idea). Concrete is close to a synonym, and cheap and temporary are unrelated.
A maverick is an independent-minded, unconventional person. Bohemian (living an unconventional, free life) is the closest. Conformist, orthodox and follower are opposites.
To meander is to follow a winding, wandering course; the opposite is to go direct (straight). Ramble is close in meaning to meander, while deputise and confirm are unrelated.
Mechanical means done by a machine. Its opposite is manual, done by hand. Automatised is close to a synonym, and yielding and surrogate are unrelated.
"Melancholy" is a deep, lasting sadness. "Excitement" and "joy" are opposites, and "aloof" means distant or unfriendly.

Mellifluous (literally "flowing like honey") describes a sweet, smooth, pleasant sound: musical. Cacophonous (harsh, jarring) is its opposite, and loud and distinct do not carry the sense of sweetness.

Memory is the faculty of remembering; oblivion is the state of forgetting or being forgotten, its opposite. Retrospection (looking back on the past) is close to memory, and suppress and impart are verbs unrelated in meaning.
Mendacious means untruthful or lying. Dishonest, fraudulent and deceitful are near-synonyms; truthful is the opposite.

words.sentence: He studied \(\underline{\text{mensuration}}\) carefully.
words.solution: Answer: A. Mensuration is the act/process of measurement.

words.sentence: Mohan has \(\underline{\text{mercurial}}\) temperament.
words.solution: Answer: A. 'Mercurial' = subject to sudden, unpredictable changes of mood; volatile. 'Volatile' is the exact synonym.
Merit is the quality of being good or worthy of praise, which is a virtue. Fatigue is tiredness, residue is what is left over, and oblique means slanting or indirect.

words.sentence: I was completely \(\underline{\text{mesmerised}}\) by the performance.
words.solution: To be mesmerised is to be held spellbound, that is, fascinated. Bored, irritated and annoyed are the opposite kind of reaction.

words.sentence: Her room looks very \(\underline{\text{messy}}\)
words.solution: Messy means untidy or disordered; its opposite is organised (neat, in order). Untidy, chaotic and disordered are synonyms of messy.

words.sentence: Operating on a child with cancer needs \(\underline{\text{meticulous}}\) planning and teamwork.
words.solution: 'Meticulous' means showing great attention to detail. 'Scrupulous' is the closest synonym, meaning careful and thorough. Matches option D: scrupulous.

words.sentence: His views on the subject are \(\underline{\text{microscopic}}\).
words.solution: 'Microscopic' means extremely small or narrow; its antonym in context of views is 'broad-based' (wide-ranging). Matches option A: broad-based.
"Mighty" means very strong and powerful; its opposite is "weak". "Forcible" and "forceful" are close to its meaning, and "haughty" means arrogant.

words.sentence: The experts' \(\underline{\text{minute}}\) examination brought to light some important clues.
words.solution: 'Minute' (adjective) means extremely small or precise; here it means very detailed. Matches option B: detailed.
Miraculous means so extraordinary as to seem like a miracle, which is incredible. Expected and average are near-opposites, and draining (exhausting) is unrelated.
Misanthropic means disliking or distrusting people in general, which is closest to antisocial. Humanitarian, sociable and philanthropic are its opposites.

words.sentence: There are a few \(\underline{\text{miscellaneous}}\) items to discuss in this meeting.
words.solution: Miscellaneous means consisting of various types mixed together; the antonym is homogenous (uniform, of the same kind). Matches option C: homogenous.
Miserable means very unhappy; its opposite is cheerful. Restrained, settled and melodious do not describe the opposite feeling.

words.sentence: This world is full of \(\underline{\text{miseries}}\).
words.solution: The word 'miseries' means conditions of great distress or suffering; 'great suffering' is the direct synonym. Matches option C: great suffering.

words.sentence: For many, a warming climatic system is expected to impact the availability of basic necessities like freshwater, food security, and energy, while efforts to redress climate change, both through adaptation and \(\underline{\text{mitigation}}\), will similarly inform and shape the global development agenda.
words.solution: Mitigation is the act of making something less severe; in climate policy it means reducing emissions and so the scale of the change. Reduction is the synonym. Cure goes too far (removing the problem altogether), and rise is the opposite.

words.sentence: His **modest** nature made all the difference.
words.solution: A modest person is unassuming and does not boast; of the options, shy (reserved, retiring) comes closest. Courageous, horrific and dry are unrelated.

words.sentence: The seminar which Ravi organised proved to be \(\underline{\text{momentous}}\) event.
words.solution: Answer: A. 'Momentous' means of great importance; its opposite is 'trivial' (unimportant).

words.sentence: The repetitive and \(\underline{\text{monotonous}}\) task of data entry made the work seem incredibly long and tedious.
words.solution: "Monotonous" means dull and unvarying; its opposite is "interesting". "Pious" means religious, "precarious" means unsafe or unstable, and "threatening" means menacing.

words.sentence: The achievements of the team have been \(\underline{\text{monumental}}\) in the last ten years.
words.solution: 'Monumental' means impressively large or great; its antonym is 'unimpressive'. Options A, B, C are synonyms or related positives. Matches option D: unimpressive.
Morbid means having an unhealthy interest in gloomy or unpleasant subjects such as death, so gloomy is the closest. Blithe (cheerful, carefree) is nearly the opposite; grand and bet are unrelated.

words.sentence: She sat there looking \(\underline{\text{morose}}\).
words.solution: Answer: A. Morose means gloomy and sullen, so cheerful is its opposite. Melancholic and sullen are synonyms of it.

words.sentence: A strong man is a mediator between divine and **mortal** fate.
words.solution: Mortal can mean deadly or causing death (a mortal wound), and lethal means the same. Delightful, sincere and overjoyed have no link to the word.

words.sentence: The diagnosis based on radiological evidence determined the condition to be \(\underline{\text{mortiferous}}\).
words.solution: Answer: C. Mortiferous means death-bringing or fatal, so in a medical context benign is its opposite. Lethal is an exact synonym and so is the trap option.
To mourn is to feel or show deep sorrow, especially for someone who has died; "grieve" means the same. "Dread" is to fear, "amuse" is to entertain, and "approve" is to agree with.

words.sentence: Planets \(\underline{\text{move}}\) in their orbits.
words.solution: The antonym of 'move' (to be in motion/travel) is 'stall' (to stop or cease motion). 'Rotate' and 'flow' involve motion; 'push' involves applying force. Matches option C: stall.
