words.sentence: Replace the underlined word with its synonym to make the sentence more meaningful. Narcotic drug addiction is in \(\underline{\text{vogue}}\) these days, as it is the most popular form of substance abuse.
words.solution: "In vogue" means in fashion, popular at the time, which matches "the most popular form". "Obscurity" is nearly the opposite, and "demand" and "standard" do not mean vogue.

"Voracious" means wanting great quantities of food (or of something), that is, greedy: "a voracious appetite". "Quenched" means satisfied (of thirst), "appreciate" means value, and "compensated" means paid back.

words.sentence: The explosive used is of my own formulation, and I can \(\underline{\text{vouch}}\) for its efficiency.
words.solution: To vouch for something is to confirm or guarantee it. Certify and witness are close in meaning and maintain (assert) is similar; invalidate (show to be false or void) is the opposite.

words.sentence: From the outset of the pandemic, the United Nations system mobilised early and comprehensively. It led on the global health response, provided life-saving humanitarian assistance to the most \(\underline{\text{vulnerable}}\), established instruments for rapid responses to the socio-economic impact and laid out a broad policy agenda for action on all fronts.
words.solution: Vulnerable means exposed to harm, that is, at risk. Poor is a narrower idea, and arrogant and adaptable are unrelated.

words.sentence: My energy \(\underline{\text{waned}}\) to see my college team performing poorly in the match.
words.solution: To wane is to decrease or grow weaker. Declined, dimmed and abated are synonyms; grew is the opposite.

words.sentence: People argue about why Venus is so much \(\underline{\text{warmer}}\) than the Earth.
words.solution: The antonym of 'warmer' (higher temperature) is 'colder' (lower temperature). Matches option B: colder.
To wax is to grow or increase (as the moon waxes). To wane is to decrease or decline, so wane is the opposite. Polish is a meaning of wax as a noun or verb, not its opposite.

words.sentence: In the question four alternatives are given for the underlined word in the sentence. Choose the alternative which best expresses the opposite meaning of the word. “Well, what if it is? You are not afraid of anything, you know,” returned the boy, looking \(\underline{\text{wicked}}\).
words.solution: "Wicked" means evil or morally wrong; its opposite is "righteous", morally right. "Evil" and "improper" are close to its meaning, and "clean" is unrelated.

words.sentence: Malaria is a \(\underline{\text{widespread}}\) disease.
words.solution: The key concept is antonym identification. 'Widespread' means found over a large area; its antonym is 'rare'. Matches option D: rare.

words.sentence: I have thus far sketched the events of my life, but I have not shown how much I have depended on books not only for pleasure and for the \(\underline{\text{wisdom}}\) they bring to all who read, but also for that knowledge which comes to others through their eyes and their ears.
words.solution: Wisdom is deep understanding and sound judgement; insight (a deep understanding of things) is the closest. Folly is its opposite, and clarity and emotion do not mean understanding.

words.sentence: The door was ajar and a faint \(\underline{\text{wisp}}\) of smoke floated through it.
words.solution: A wisp is a small, thin amount of something (a wisp of smoke or hair). Its opposite is a large amount, "a lot". A trickle is also a small amount, so it is close in meaning, and itchy and wind are unrelated.

words.sentence: There prevailed a \(\underline{\text{woebegone}}\) feeling in the room.
words.solution: Answer: B. 'Woebegone' means sorrowful/sad. Its antonym is 'Cheerful'.
Wonderful means extremely good or inspiring delight, the same as amazing. Awful is its opposite; synthetic (man-made) and upright (honest, or vertical) are unrelated.

words.sentence: \(\underline{\text{Wooing}}\) everyone over an issue for support will not serve much purpose.
words.solution: Answer: A. 'Wooing' means seeking to win over or persuade; its opposite is 'discouraging'. Encouraging/pursuing/persuading are close in meaning.

words.sentence: His lectures are often \(\underline{\text{wordy}}\) and pointless.
words.solution: Answer: B. Antonym of 'wordy' (using too many words) is 'concise' (brief). Diffuse, garrulous and voluble are synonyms of wordy.

words.sentence: He has been \(\underline{\text{yearning}}\) to go home.
words.solution: The synonym of 'yearning' (longing intensely for something) is 'hankering' (craving). Matches option D: hankering.

words.sentence: One should not \(\underline{\text{yell}}\) at children.
words.solution: To yell is to shout loudly; the opposite is to whisper, to speak very softly. Notify, indemnify and terrorise are not opposites of yell.

words.sentence: The salesman \(\underline{\text{yielded}}\) to the demands of his corrupt boss.
words.solution: To yield to demands is to give in to them, that is to concede. Courted means sought favour, hounded means harassed, and trended is unrelated.
Zany means amusingly unconventional or crazy. Bizarre, clownish and eccentric are near-synonyms; sensible is the opposite.
Zealous means full of eager, enthusiastic devotion. Detached, apathetic and indifferent all mean lacking interest, the opposite.
